reader_title: Industrial districts allow data centers by right
summary: A data center is a permitted use in the Light Industrial, Industrial and Planned Industrial districts. The table also marks the Airport Overlay; check the underlying zone and airport standards. Other permits can still be required.
locator: September 2026 ordinance, Table 4.1, pp. 49 and 58; §4.17(B), p. 33
district: LI, I and PID; AO overlay

reader_title: What Greene County calls a data center
summary: The county definition covers large computer systems that store and process data for off-site users. It lists generators, batteries, cooling and fire suppression as typical support equipment. The definition alone does not establish allowed locations.
locator: November 9, 2026 edition, definition of DATA CENTER, p. 165
evidence: storage and processing for off-site users

reader_title: Data centers are allowed in the Regional Enterprise Park district
summary: Franklin County lists data centers alongside call centers and offices in its Regional Enterprise Park district. This answers the land-use question for that district; it does not issue a permit for an individual building.
